reasons: Classification is correct: the grant in 2.1/2.2 is perpetual and irrevocable and 14.1 permits assignment to an M&A successor, but neither Section 2 nor the definitions extend the licence to Corio's affiliates or to contractors acting on its behalf, and no mechanism exists to add them. That fails the fallback's material affiliate-coverage requirement (and edges into the walk-away 'affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them'), so a deviation rather than a compliant-at-fallback call is justified.

Redline is minimal and actionable: instead of rewriting both grant clauses, it inserts a single new Section 2.11 at the end of Section 2 extending the Section 2 licences to affiliates and contractors with Corio responsible for their compliance — exactly the redline guidance, and it leaves the already-acceptable irrevocability and successor-transfer language untouched.

Drafting is technically sound: lowercase 'affiliates' avoids relying on an undefined 'Affiliate' term, the placement after 2.10 sits inside the grant section, and the extension is framed as the licences 'extending' rather than an assignment, so it does not collide with the 'nontransferable (except per 14.1)' qualifier.

Comment is accurate, in-house voice, carries the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why in two sentences, and offers the written-notice fallback without lecturing. Deterministic checks (operation applies, affiliates covered, no at-will revocation) are all consistent with the rendered edit.
